title: Bidirectional A* in San Francisco: Millisecond Routes ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from start and goal simultaneously on a real-map style grid. It meets in the middle to cut search space fast—just like autonomous vehicle routing tries to do in milliseconds.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm—How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

In this visualization, two A* searches run at once: one forward from the start, one backward from the goal. Each uses a heuristic (think: “how far to go”) to expand the most promising frontier first, but both halves converge so you explore far fewer nodes than classic A*.

Takeaway: Bidirectional A* = faster graph search when you can score progress from both ends (same road network, smaller explored area, quicker convergence).

Debate question: Should real routing always prioritize speed (fewer expansions) or path smoothness (fewer turns) even if it means more computation?

fb_caption:
Bidirectional A* is a graph search strategy where we run A* from the start and the goal at the same time, meeting in the middle to reduce the number of expanded nodes. That’s why it can feel “instant” for real-world routing—especially when paired with strong heuristics.
